source_review.notes: Checked current OAuth security BCP RFC 9700; JWT access-token profile RFC 9068; JWT BCP RFC 8725; JWT RFC 7519; OpenID Connect Core errata set 2; OAuth token exchange RFC 8693; and DPoP RFC 9449.

evidence: Reviewed partial context-construction function, issuer-subject principal pair, context tuple, actor chain, and privilege-monotonicity notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All symbols are defined and TeX remains inside GitHub-supported delimiters.

evidence: Executed valid, wrong-token-type, wrong-audience, exact-expiry, and missing-subject cases; each reached the intended policy result.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The exact expiry boundary rejects when exp is equal to validation time.

evidence: Checked conjunctive validation, issuer-subject namespacing, audience-specific derivation, actor-chain preservation, and non-increasing effective privilege across hops.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Cross-audience privilege comparison is explicitly limited to policy-aware mappings.

evidence: Reviewed unsigned and wrong-kind tokens, algorithm confusion, wrong issuer/audience, time boundaries, sender replay, tenant mismatch, header spoofing, key rotation floods, introspection outage, impersonation, asynchronous expiry, revocation, privacy, and downstream audience mismatch.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Credential, identity-role, trust-hop, time, delegation, privacy, and operational boundaries are separated.

evidence: Checked full profile verification, immutable typed context, distinct user/client/workload/tenant fields, no body override, least-privilege audience exchange, immediate workload authentication, actor provenance, secret redaction, and durable-job handling throughout.
invariant_checking.notes: Authentication evidence is never treated as final object-level authorization.

proof_review.notes: No cryptographic theorem or universal security proof is claimed.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; equations define security invariants and evidence scope.

evidence: The executable checker explicitly disclaims decoding, signature verification, key retrieval, sender binding, and authorization; unit, integration, operational drill, and deployed-hop evidence remain distinct.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Passing claim checks do not establish cryptographic validity or permission.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed identity roles, credential distrust, validation profiles, authentication/authorization separation, context construction and provenance, resource-bound validation, workload/user pairing, delegation, audience/sender restriction, key and time handling, asynchronous work, observability, failures, and trust-chain tests.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed access versus ID token confusion, issuer metadata, algorithm configuration, key rotation and abuse, token exchange, sender constraint, ingress header stripping, workload authentication, token custody, revocation, broker failure, audit, and privacy minimization.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed one-page retrieval, one executable policy-boundary audit, ten distinct worked examples, and five exercises progressing from identity classification through validation trace, diagnosis, architecture comparison, and delayed impersonation transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
